newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says will review public financial firms.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says will review public financial firms.

text.p: Japan's moves to carry out overall reforms of its financial markets would inevitably involve a review of public financial institutions, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told a parliamentary committee on Friday.

"As reforms proceed, the role of the private sector institutions would be strengthened and expanded. We cannot avoid reviewing the role and functions of public institutions and their source of income," Hashimoto said.
He added that the government may also review government agencies which operate on funds from these public firms.
Public financial institutions, such as postal savings, have been criticised for robbing business away from private firms.

Funds collected by postal savings and the public pension system are funnelled into the government's Fiscal and Investment and Loan Programme -- known as the country's "second budget" -- from which government agencies are given funds to make loans for public works and other projects.
